question: A teacher asks the class a question. How long do they usually wait before answering it themselves or calling on someone?
answer: About one second, in Mary Budd Rowe's recordings of science lessons. When teachers learned to wait three seconds or more, answers grew longer, more pupils spoke, and they offered more reasons. One second is too short to think: the quick talkers fill it.
move: After asking a question, count to three before you speak again.
ask: Do I answer my own questions before anyone else can?
reference: Rowe, Wait-time and rewards as instructional variables, their influence on language, logic, and fate control: Part one, wait-time, Journal of Research in Science Teaching 11(2), 1974; Rowe, Wait time: slowing down may be a way of speeding up, Journal of Teacher Education 37(1), 1986
